name: v_z
prose: v_z(sp, vp), v_z.c:29-124, implements vi's z command and returns 0 or 1. With VC_C1SET it takes lno = vp->count, replaced by the last line (db_last) if that line does not exist (return 1 if db_last fails); otherwise lno = vp->m_start.lno. It sets vp->m_final to (lno, vp->m_start.cno). If VC_C2SET is set and count2 is nonzero it caps count2 at O_WINDOW and calls vs_crel (return 1 on failure). It then switches on vp->character: '-' calls vs_sm_fill(sp, lno, P_BOTTOM) and '.' calls it with P_MIDDLE; '+' with VC_C1SET calls vs_sm_fill(P_TOP) then vs_sm_position(sp, &vp->m_final, 0, P_TOP), without VC_C1SET calls vs_sm_scroll(sp, &vp->m_final, sp->t_rows, Z_PLUS); '^' with VC_C1SET calls vs_sm_fill(P_BOTTOM), vs_sm_position(P_TOP) and vs_sm_fill(sp, vp->m_final.lno, P_BOTTOM), without it vs_sm_scroll(..., Z_CARAT); for any other character it returns 1 with a usage message unless the key is CR or NL, which calls vs_sm_fill(P_TOP). Any failing vs_* call returns 1. On success it returns 0. In the '+' and '^' cases vs_sm_position or vs_sm_scroll may change vp->m_final, so m_final is not always (lno, m_start.cno).

prose: vs_number(sp), vs_line.c:485-536 (the packet name v_number is vs_number in the file), repaints the line numbers and always returns 0. name: vs_sm_fill
prose: vs_sm_fill(sp, lno, pos), vs_smap.c:172-286, rebuilds the screen map and returns 0 or 1. It first flushes every SMAP entry (sp->t_rows entries from HMAP) and sets SC_SCR_REDRAW. By pos: P_FILL decides by distance (vs_sm_nlines against HALFTEXT) between anchoring line 1 at the top (lno set to 1, goto top), anchoring the last line (from db_last, return 1 if it fails) at the bottom, and the middle. P_TOP anchors HMAP at lno with coff 0 and soff 1, or, when lno is OOBLNO, keeps the current HMAP line and resets soff to 1 if the line now has fewer screens than HMAP->soff, then fills downward over the map with vs_sm_next (each entry from the previous). P_MIDDLE puts lno in the entry t_rows / 2, fills upward with vs_sm_prev (on failure it sets lno = 1 and goes to the top case) and then downward with vs_sm_next. P_BOTTOM anchors TMAP at lno (or leaves TMAP when lno is OOBLNO) and fills upward with vs_sm_prev (on failure falls back to the top case with lno = 1). Any other pos calls abort(). A vs_sm_next failure in the downward fills goes to err, which restarts the map from line 1 (HMAP = line 1, filled downward with vs_sm_next) and returns 0 if that succeeds or 1 if even that fails. A normal fill returns 0.

name: vs_sm_down
prose: Static function vs_sm_down(sp, rp, count, scmd, smp), vs_smap.c:807-952, scrolls the screen map down (towards earlier lines) and sets the cursor mark; it returns 0 or 1. It returns 1 after v_sof if HMAP is already line 1 at its first screen (or O_LEFTRIGHT) and scmd is CNTRL_Y or Z_CARAT or smp == HMAP. cursor_set starts as scmd == CNTRL_Y. For a small screen (IS_SMALL): if count >= sp->t_maxrows or scmd is CNTRL_B it erases the screen, steps back count lines with vs_sm_prev (stopping at line 1), refills with vs_sm_fill(OOBLNO, P_TOP) and returns the result of vs_sm_position(sp, rp, 0, P_BOTTOM), returning 1 on any failure; otherwise it sets cursor_set = (scmd == CNTRL_Y) || vs_sm_cursor(...), grows t_rows with vs_sm_1down up to t_maxrows (stopping at line 1), sets rp from the saved cursor entry when cursor_set is false, and returns 0 if count reached 0. The main loop scrolls one line at a time with vs_sm_1down (return 1 on failure, stop at line 1), moving smp for CNTRL_Y (setting ychanged when smp is already at TMAP) and Z_CARAT. After it, if scmd is not CNTRL_Y and cursor_set is true it returns 0 without setting rp in this part of the function. Then by scmd: CNTRL_B picks the last existing line on the map when count was exhausted (else falls into CNTRL_U), CNTRL_U moves smp up by count entries (clamped to HMAP), CNTRL_Y sets rp from smp only if ychanged and returns 0 (so rp can be left unset when ychanged is 0), Z_CARAT leaves smp, anything else calls abort(). For the remaining cases it calls vs_line on smp if its cache is not valid (return 1 on failure), sets rp->lno = smp->lno and rp->cno to 0 or the saved column, and returns 0.

name: vs_vsplit
prose: vs_vsplit(sp, new), vs_split.c:203-286, splits sp vertically into sp and new and returns 0 or 1. If sp->cols / 2 <= MINIMUM_SCREEN_COLS it queues an error message and returns 1 without changing anything (so a split needs sp->cols / 2 > MINIMUM_SCREEN_COLS). Otherwise it calls vs_resolve(sp, NULL, 1), allocates new's screen map (CALLOC; return 1 if it fails) and initialises its first entry to line sp->lno, coff 0, soff 1. It sets cols = sp->cols / 2, new->cols = sp->cols - cols - 1, sp->cols = cols, new->coff = sp->coff + cols + 1 and sp->cno = 0, copies rows, t_rows, t_maxrows, t_minrows, roff and defscroll from sp to new, sets new's TMAP to the last entry, inserts new in the screen list with vs_insert, calls gp->scr_split(sp, new) (result ignored), sets SC_SCR_REFORMAT | SC_STATUS on sp, and sets SC_SCR_REFORMAT | SC_STATUS plus the SC_EX, SC_VI, SC_SCR_VI, SC_SCR_EX and SC_READONLY bits copied from sp on new. It returns 0.

name: vs_resize
prose: vs_resize(sp, count, adj), vs_split.c:795-905, moves rows between sp and a neighbouring screen and returns 0 or 1. It returns 0 immediately, changing nothing, if count is 0, or if adj is A_SET and count equals sp->t_maxrows; for other A_SET it becomes A_DECREASE or A_INCREASE with count set to the difference from t_maxrows. It finds next, the first later screen in the list that overlaps sp horizontally, and prev likewise before sp, and sets either to NULL unless it has exactly sp's coff and cols. For A_DECREASE (a negative count is negated) s = sp: if sp->t_maxrows < MINIMUM_SCREEN_ROWS + count it queues "The screen can only shrink to %d rows" and returns 1; g = prev with s_off = count, else g = next with g_off = -count, and if neither exists it queues "The screen cannot shrink" and returns 1. For A_INCREASE g = sp: s = next if next is large enough (s_off = count), otherwise s = prev (if none: "The screen cannot grow" and return 1; if prev is too small the 'can only shrink' message and return 1) with g_off = -count. Then s->rows -= count and s->roff += s_off, g->rows += count and g->roff += g_off (so with A_DECREASE where g is next, s_off is 0 and sp->roff is unchanged), g's t_rows, t_maxrows and TMAP grow by count (t_minrows too when it equalled t_maxrows), s's t_rows and t_maxrows shrink by count (t_minrows clamped), TMAP of s is moved back, and both get SC_SCR_REFORMAT | SC_STATUS. It calls gp->scr_discard(0, list) with g and s (result ignored) and returns 0.

name: poll_cq
prose: Static function poll_cq(wq, cq, cqe, cqe_flushed, cookie, credit), cq.c:345-549 (Chelsio T4), reaps one completion queue entry and returns 0, -EAGAIN or the error from t4_next_cqe. It first sets *cqe_flushed = 0 and *credit = 0 (credit is not set to any other value in this function), then calls t4_next_cqe(cq, &hw_cqe) and returns that error at once, consuming nothing, if it is nonzero. If wq is NULL it skips the CQE (ret = -EAGAIN). For a FW_RI_READ_RESP opcode it skips with -EAGAIN for an egress-error read response (setting the wq in error when the status is nonzero), for a WRID_STAG of 1, or when the oldest read is not signaled (after advance_oldest_read); otherwise it synthesises a read-request CQE and advances the oldest read. A FW_RI_TERMINATE opcode is skipped with -EAGAIN. If the CQE status is nonzero or the wq is in error it sets *cqe_flushed to (status == T4_ERR_SWFLUSH), sets wq->error and processes the CQE. For an RQ-type CQE it sets the wq in error and skips with -EAGAIN if the RQ is empty, and marks a T4_ERR_MSN status when the MSN differs from wq->rq.msn. An SQ CQE whose index is not the SQ consumer index and is not a software CQE is recorded as complete in sw_sq and skipped with -EAGAIN after flush_completed_wrs. In the processing step it copies the CQE to *cqe; for an SQ CQE it updates in_use and cidx, sets *cookie to the work request id and consumes the SQ entry, then runs flush_completed_wrs; for an RQ CQE it sets *cookie to the RQ work request id and consumes the RQ entry. At skip_cqe it consumes the software or hardware CQE (t4_swcq_consume or t4_hwcq_consume) and returns ret, which is 0 after a processed CQE and -EAGAIN after every skip path. The BUG_ON checks mean some inconsistent states abort rather than return.

name: mad_rpc
prose: mad_rpc(port, rpc, dport, payload, rcvdata), rpc.c:221-284, sends one MAD and returns rcvdata on success or NULL. For MAD RPC version 1 classes it first sets rpcv1->error = 0. In a loop it zeroes the send buffer and builds the packet with mad_build_pkt (a negative result returns NULL, leaving rpcv1->error at 0 and rpc->rstatus unchanged), then calls _do_madrpc with the class agent, timeout and retries; if that returns a negative value it copies the local error variable into rpcv1->error (version 1 only; what _do_madrpc stores in it was not read), logs a warning and returns NULL, again without setting rpc->rstatus. It reads the reply status from the MAD header; if the status equals IB_MAD_STS_REDIRECT it calls redirect_port and repeats the loop when that returns 0, otherwise (redirect_port nonzero, or any non-redirect status) it leaves the loop. After the loop, for version 1 classes it sets rpcv1->error = error (the value from the last _do_madrpc call), and it sets rpc->rstatus = status. If status is nonzero (including a redirect that could not be followed) it logs the error, sets errno = EIO and returns NULL. Otherwise it optionally dumps the data when ibdebug is set, copies rpc->datasz bytes from the reply at offset rpc->dataoffs into rcvdata if rcvdata is non-NULL, and returns rcvdata (so NULL on success when rcvdata is NULL).

name: group_nodes
prose: group_nodes(fabric), chassis.c:1237-1344 (the packet name was an unnamed enclosing function), groups the fabric's nodes into chassis and returns 0 on success or -1 on failure. It starts with an empty local chassis_scan and chassisnum = 0. Pass 1 walks fabric->switches: for a Voltaire vendor id it calls fill_voltaire_chassis_record and for a Mellanox vendor id fill_mellanox_chassis_record, jumping to cleanup if either returns nonzero. Pass 2 walks the switches again: for each Voltaire node that has ch_found set, is a spine (is_spine) and does not already have a chassis with a chassisnum, it calls add_chassis (cleanup on failure), gives the new current chassis the next chassisnum and calls build_chassis (cleanup on failure). Pass 3 walks fabric->nodes, skipping Voltaire nodes: for each node with a nonzero System GUID it looks up an existing chassis with find_chassisguid and increments its nodecount, or else calls add_chassis (cleanup on failure), records get_chassisguid(node) and nodecount 1 on the new chassis and sets fabric->chassis to the first chassis if it is still NULL. Pass 4 walks fabric->nodes again, skipping Voltaire nodes: for a node with a nonzero System GUID whose chassis has nodecount > 1 it assigns the next chassisnum to the chassis if it has none, then, if the node is not yet marked ch_found, marks it and calls add_node_to_chassis, or, if it is already marked and is a Mellanox node, calls insert_mellanox_line_and_spine. On success it sets fabric->chassis = chassis_scan.first_chassis and returns 0. At cleanup it frees every chassis in the local list starting at chassis_scan.first_chassis (only the chassis structures themselves), sets fabric->chassis = NULL and returns -1; failures of the fill_* and build_chassis calls therefore also lead to -1, not only add_chassis.

name: mlx5_start_poll
prose: Static inline function mlx5_start_poll(ibcq, attr, lock, stall, cqe_version), cq.c:831-894 (mlx5 extended CQ polling), starts a poll and returns 0, EINVAL, ENOENT or an error from mlx5_parse_lazy_cqe. It returns EINVAL at once if attr->comp_mask is nonzero. If stall is nonzero it first stalls before taking the lock: in adaptive mode, if cq->stall_last_count is nonzero it calls mlx5_stall_cycles_poll_cq with last count plus stall_cycles; in the other mode, if cq->stall_next_poll is set it clears it and calls mlx5_stall_poll_cq. If lock is nonzero it takes cq->lock, then sets cq->cur_rsc and cq->cur_srq to NULL and calls mlx5_get_next_cqe. If that returns CQ_EMPTY it releases the lock if it took it, and when stall is nonzero updates the stall state (adaptive: stall_cycles = max(stall_cycles - mlx5_stall_cq_dec_step, mlx5_stall_cq_poll_min) and stall_last_count set to the current cycle count; otherwise stall_next_poll = 1), then returns ENOENT. For any other result it sets MLX5_CQ_FLAGS_FOUND_CQES when stall is nonzero and calls mlx5_parse_lazy_cqe. If that returns an error it releases the lock if it took it and, when stall is nonzero, in adaptive mode lowers stall_cycles the same way and sets stall_last_count = 0 (the non-adaptive mode changes no stall counter), and in both modes clears FOUND_CQES; it returns the parse result, so on success (0) the lock stays held for the matching end_poll.

name: rdma_migrate_id
prose: rdma_migrate_id(id, channel), cma.c:2255-2308 (the packet name ucma_migrate_id is rdma_migrate_id in the file), moves an rdma_cm_id to another event channel and returns 0 or an error. It returns ERR(EINVAL) if id_priv->sync is set and channel is NULL (a synchronous id cannot move to a new private channel). If channel is NULL it creates a private channel with rdma_create_event_channel (sync = 1) and returns -1, not ENOMEM, if that fails. It builds a MIGRATE_ID command with the id handle and the current channel's fd (id->channel->fd) and writes it to channel->fd; if the write does not return the full command size it destroys the channel it created when sync is set and returns ERR(ENODATA) for a short non-negative count or -1 for a negative result. On success, if id_priv->sync was set it acks and clears id->event when present and destroys the old id->channel. It then takes id_priv->mut, sets id_priv->sync = sync and id->channel = channel, waits on id_priv->cond while id_priv->events_completed < resp.events_reported, releases the mutex and returns 0.

prose: Static function server_open(rs, msg), rcopy.c:229-271, handles a received CMD_OPEN and returns an int status. It prints "opening: ". If the global file_addr is non-NULL or the global fd is greater than 0 it prints a message and goes to out with ret = EBUSY. Otherwise it prints the path and calls open(path, O_RDWR | O_CREAT | O_TRUNC, msg->data) into the global fd; if that fails it prints a message and stores errno in ret, but line 264 then sets ret = 0 unconditionally, so the function reports 0 even when the open failed (fd stays negative). At out it frees path if allocated, calls msg_send_resp(rs, msg, ret) and returns ret. The path buffer is not NUL-terminated by this function (printf of it assumes the sender included the NUL).

name: copysockopts
prose: Static function copysockopts(dfd, sfd, dapi, sapi), preload.c:447-474, copies a few socket settings from sfd to dfd using the two socket_calls tables, and returns 0 or the failing call's nonzero result. It reads sfd's file status flags with sapi->fcntl(sfd, F_GETFL); if the result is positive it sets them on dfd with dapi->fcntl(dfd, F_SETFL, flags) and uses that call's result; a nonzero final result (including a negative F_GETFL result) is returned at once, while a result of 0 from F_GETFL continues without copying flags. It then reads SO_REUSEADDR from sfd with getsockopt and, if the value is nonzero and the getsockopt returned 0, sets it on dfd with setsockopt; a nonzero result is returned. The same is done for TCP_NODELAY at the IPPROTO_TCP level. The tested value param is read even when getsockopt failed (the test is param && !ret, so param is uninitialised on the first failure path but ret is then returned anyway). A zero option value is not copied. It returns 0 if none of the attempted calls failed. The returned failure value is whatever the socket_calls entry returned (typically -1), not an errno code.

prose: rsocket(domain, type, protocol), rsocket.c:1130-1170, creates an rsocket and returns its index, or a negative value. It calls rs_configure and rs_alloc(NULL, type), returning ERR(ENOMEM) if that fails. For SOCK_STREAM it calls rdma_create_id (RDMA_PS_TCP), sets the cm_id's source address family to domain and uses the event channel fd as the index; for SOCK_DGRAM it calls ds_init(rs, domain) and uses rs->udp_sock as the index. A nonzero rdma_create_id or ds_init result, or a negative rs_insert(rs, index) result, goes to err, which calls rs_free(rs) and returns that value. On success it returns rs->index.

name: raccept
prose: raccept(socket, addr, addrlen), rsocket.c:1226-1282, accepts a connection on a listening rsocket and returns the new rsocket index or a failing value. It returns ERR(EBADF) if the socket is not registered and ERR(ENOMEM) if rs_alloc(rs, rs->type) fails. It then calls rdma_get_request(rs->cm_id, &new_rs->cm_id), rs_insert on the new cm_id's channel fd, and checks the connection data version; failures go to err (the negative rs_insert result, ERR(ENOTSUP) if creq->version != 1, or rdma_get_request's result). If the listening rsocket has O_NONBLOCK it sets O_NONBLOCK on the new cm_id's channel fd. It calls rs_create_ep (error goes to err), saves the connection data, builds the accept parameters with the response connection data and calls rdma_accept: a result of 0 sets new_rs->state = rs_connect_rdwr; a nonzero result with errno EAGAIN or EWOULDBLOCK sets new_rs->state = rs_accepting and is treated as success; any other nonzero result goes to err (and the value returned is rdma_accept's, typically -1). name: rs_poll_cq
prose: Static function rs_poll_cq(rs), rsocket.c:1900-1986, drains the receive completion queue (rs->cm_id->recv_cq) one completion at a time and returns 0 or a negative value. For a receive completion with a non-success status it skips it (not counted). For a successful one it increments rcnt and takes the message from the immediate data or from the receive buffer area, then by operation: RS_OP_SGL sets rs->sseq_comp; RS_OP_IOMAP_SGL and RS_OP_WRITE do nothing; RS_OP_CTRL with RS_CTRL_DISCONNECT sets rs->state = rs_disconnected and returns 0 at once; with RS_CTRL_SHUTDOWN it clears rs_readable if the rsocket is writable, otherwise sets rs_disconnected and returns 0 at once; any other operation is appended to the rmsg ring at rmsg_tail. The two immediate returns skip the reposting of receive buffers and leave later completions unread. For a send completion it updates counters by the operation (SGL: ctrl_max_seqno++; CTRL: ctrl_max_seqno++ and, for RS_CTRL_DISCONNECT, state = rs_disconnected without returning; IOMAP_SGL and other ops: sqe_avail++ and sbuf_bytes_avail adjusted), and if the status is not success while the state has rs_connected it sets state = rs_error and err = EIO, then continues the loop. After the loop (ret is ibv_poll_cq's last result: 0 when the queue is empty, negative on error), if the state still has rs_connected it reposts rcnt receive buffers with rs_post_recv while ret is 0 (so none are reposted after a negative poll result), and if ret is nonzero it sets state = rs_error and err = errno. It returns ret.

name: __osmv_dispatch_rmpp_rcv
prose: Static function __osmv_dispatch_rmpp_rcv(h_bind, p_mad, p_txn, p_mad_addr), osm_vendor_mlx_dispatcher.c:484-637 (the earlier hit at line 83 is the prototype), handles one received RMPP segment of an existing transaction and returns an ib_api_status_t (initially IB_SUCCESS). An RMPP ACK is logged and dropped (returns IB_SUCCESS). An ABORT or STOP from the peer returns IB_REMOTE_ERROR. Otherwise it calls __osmv_dispatch_accept_seg and switches on its status: IB_SUCCESS computes is_last1 from the segment's last flag and is_last2 from the accumulated byte count against the size announced in the first segment; if they differ it sends an ABORT/BAD_LEN NAK and returns IB_ERROR; otherwise it sends an ACK (__osmv_dispatch_send_ack) and continues. IB_INSUFFICIENT_RESOURCES (an out-of-order segment) sends an ACK and returns IB_SUCCESS without accepting it. IB_INSUFFICIENT_MEMORY sends a STOP/RESX NAK and returns IB_INSUFFICIENT_MEMORY. Any other status triggers CL_ASSERT(FALSE) and then falls out of the switch with the unexpected status, which is returned unchanged at the end (after the not-last check). If the segment is not the last one it logs that assembly continues and returns the current status (IB_SUCCESS in the normal case). For the last segment it takes the size from the first segment or, if that was 0, from the last, allocates a MADW with osm_mad_pool_get (NULL gives IB_INSUFFICIENT_MEMORY without any NAK), reassembles the MAD (a failure returns that status and does not release the MADW just allocated), calls osmv_txn_done unless the transaction was initiated by the peer and the response is a multi-response, restores the original transaction id in the MAD and calls p_bo->recv_cb(p_new_madw, cb_context, p_req_madw). It then returns the status, IB_SUCCESS after a delivered message.

name: ni_rcv_process_new
prose: Static function ni_rcv_process_new(sm, p_madw), osm_node_info_rcv.c:657-838, processes a NodeInfo reply from a newly discovered node and returns void. It reads the NodeInfo and the local port number from the SMP, logs the discovery, and returns (via Exit, with nothing created) if the local port number exceeds num_ports (non-compliant node, error logged). It creates a node with osm_node_new and returns if that fails (error logged); it creates a port with osm_port_new and, if that fails, deletes the new node and returns. It inserts the port into sm->p_subn->port_guid_tbl; if an entry with that GUID already exists it logs both directed routes, deletes the new port and node and returns without adding anything. It then creates an alias GUID object with osm_alias_guid_new: if that allocation fails it logs an error and carries on without an alias; otherwise it inserts it into alias_port_guid_tbl and, if the alias GUID is already present, logs an error and deletes only the alias object (port and node stay). If the SM state is master it sets port->is_new = 1. For a router node it creates a router object with osm_router_new and inserts it in rtr_guid_tbl; failures are only logged. It then inserts the node into node_guid_tbl: if another entry with that GUID is already there (a discovery race) it logs that, deletes the new node, sets the links on the existing node with ni_rcv_set_links and returns; otherwise it sets the links on the new node, increments its discovery_count, calls ni_rcv_get_node_desc, and calls ni_rcv_process_new_ca_or_router for CA and router nodes or ni_rcv_process_new_switch for switches; any other node type logs "Unknown node type". It does not take locks itself.

If no LID was requested or the LID names the local port, it checks that the requester shares a pkey with the local port (if not: release, log and return with no reply) and, unless the GUID, priority or state component conditions exclude the local SM, adds the local SM record with smir_rcv_new_smir. Then, if the LID named a port other than the local one, it looks that port's GUID up in sm_guid_tbl and, if found, adds its remote-SM record with sa_smir_by_comp_mask (a log message otherwise); if no LID was given at all (p_port is NULL) it applies sa_smir_by_comp_mask_cb to every entry of sm_guid_tbl. It releases the lock and calls osm_sa_respond(sa, p_madw, sizeof(ib_sminfo_record_t), &rec_list), so the reply (possibly empty) is sent when the LID was not found.

name: osm_sm_state_mgr_process
prose: osm_sm_state_mgr_process(sm, signal), osm_sm_state_mgr.c:272-499, applies a state-manager signal to the SM state machine and returns an ib_api_status_t (IB_SUCCESS unless set otherwise). name: state_mgr_is_sm_port_down
prose: Static function state_mgr_is_sm_port_down(sm), osm_state_mgr.c:434-490, returns a boolean_t TRUE when the SM's own port is considered down. It reads port_guid = sm->p_subn->sm_port_guid. If that is 0 it logs ERR 3308 and treats the state as IB_LINK_DOWN without taking sm->p_lock. Otherwise it takes sm->p_lock (CL_PLOCK_ACQUIRE) and looks the port up with osm_get_port_by_guid; if there is none it logs ERR 3309, treats the state as IB_LINK_DOWN and releases the lock. If the port exists it sets state = IB_LINK_ACTIVE when its node is a switch whose switch_info is not an enhanced port 0 (a base switch port 0), otherwise state = osm_physp_get_port_state(port's physp); then, if p_port->discovery_count is 0 it logs ERR 330A and sets state = IB_LINK_DOWN; it releases the lock. It returns state == IB_LINK_DOWN. So it returns TRUE for a zero SM port GUID, an unknown port, a port with discovery_count 0, or a non-base-port-0 port whose physical state is IB_LINK_DOWN, and FALSE otherwise; the lock is taken and released only on the paths that reach the lookup.

name: link_srcsink
prose: link_srcsink(t, i, j, k), osm_torus.c:1665-1806, moves a fabric switch's source/sink ports into the torus switch's SRCSINK port group and returns bool. It canonicalizes i, j and k against the torus dimensions and looks up tsw = t->sw[i][j][k]; if there is none it returns true. It takes fsw = tsw->tmp; if fsw is NULL or fsw->osm_switch is NULL it logs ERR 4E1C and returns false. Otherwise it sets the port group at index 2 * TORUS_MAX_DIM to type SRCSINK and transfers the osm_switch from fsw to tsw (tsw->osm_switch = fsw->osm_switch, its priv set to tsw, fsw->osm_switch set to NULL); this transfer happens before the port loop, so it also takes place on the later false returns. For each fsw port: a port of type SRCSINK is moved into the group (attached to tsw, group port count incremented, fsw->port[p] cleared); a PASSTHRU port whose link has a SRCSINK (CA) end is converted: the link is examined, and if the far end is not SRCSINK it is skipped. If the group already has portgrp_sz ports it logs ERR 4E1D or 4E1E and the function returns false; a CA end with a NULL osm_port logs ERR 4E1F and returns false; if alloc_tlink returns NULL that port is skipped (the CA link is not moved and the function still can return true); otherwise a new torus link is filled, added to the group, the CA's osm_port is handed to the new link, t->ca_cnt is incremented, and the fabric endpoint is cleared. After the loop it returns true. Earlier ports stay moved when a later port makes it return false.

name: new_size
prose: Static function new_size(size), st.c:150-171, returns the next table size from the static primes[] array for a requested bin count. In the compiled (#else) branch it starts with newsize = MINSIZE (8) and i = 0 and, for each i up to the number of entries in primes[] (29, the last entry being 0), tests newsize > size, doubling newsize each step; it returns primes[i] for the first i where 8 << i exceeds size. primes[i] is (8 << i) plus a small offset, e.g. primes[0] = 11 (for size up to 7), primes[1] = 19 (8 to 15), primes[2] = 37, primes[3] = 67, primes[17] = 1048583 (1048576 + 7, for size up to 1048575 and above 524287), and so on up to primes[27] = 1073741909 (1073741824 + 85) for sizes from 536870912 up to 1073741823. For a negative size it returns primes[0]. If no entry qualifies (size at least 1073741824, or the int newsize shift overflows) it falls out of the loop and returns 0 (the comment says it should raise an exception); the int doubling past 2^30 is signed overflow in C, so the exact behaviour for such sizes is not defined by the language. The #if 0 branch (a power-of-two version returning -1) is not compiled.

name: regexpr
prose: regexpr(), lex.c:561-592, scans the body of a /regular expression/ in the awk lexer and returns REGEXPR (via the RET macro). It uses a static heap buffer buf (initially 500 bytes, allocated on first use with FATAL "out of space for reg expr" if malloc fails) that is reused across calls. It reads characters with input() until a '/' or end of input (0). Before storing each character it calls adjbuf to make room (FATAL if that fails). A newline ends the scan: it terminates the buffer, reports SYNTAX "newline in regular expression", pushes the newline back with unput and breaks out of the loop. A backslash stores itself and the next input() character (the next character is stored without further checks, including a newline or 0). Any other character is stored. After the loop it terminates the buffer; if the loop ended on end of input (c == 0) it reports SYNTAX "non-terminated regular expression". It then sets yylval.s to tostring(buf), a fresh heap copy that the caller owns, calls unput('/') so the next input() returns '/', and returns REGEXPR. In the newline case the '/' is therefore read before the pushed-back newline. FATAL (malloc, adjbuf, tostring) ends the program, and unput may itself call FATAL if its pushback buffer is full (not read, so not verified); SYNTAX reports an error and the function carries on.

name: get_str_val
prose: Static function get_str_val(vp, fmt), tran.c:424-513, returns vp->sval for the awk Cell vp, converting a number to a string when needed; fmt points to the OFMT or CONVFMT format-string pointer. If neither NUM nor STR is set in vp->tval it calls funnyvar (not read). If vp is a field and fields have not been split yet it calls fldbld(), else if it is the record and the record is not built it calls recbld(). If vp is not a string (isstr is false) it converts with the update_str_val macro: frees the old sval if freeable, then formats fval as "+inf"/"-inf"/"+nan"/"-nan" for non-finite values (get_inf_nan), as "%.30g" if the value is integral, otherwise with *fmt into a 256-byte buffer; stores a tostring copy in sval, clears DONTFREE and sets STR; then it sets CONVO (clearing CONVC) when fmt == OFMT or CONVC (clearing CONVO) otherwise, and vp->fmt = *fmt. If vp is already a string it returns the existing string unchanged when it is DONTFREE, is not numeric (isnum false) or is a field. Otherwise (a string that is also numeric, not DONTFREE, not a field) it reconverts with update_str_val when the cached conversion was made with the other kind of format (for fmt == OFMT: CONVC set, or CONVO set with vp->fmt != *fmt; for the CONVFMT case: CONVO set, or CONVC set with vp->fmt != *fmt), updating the CONV flag and vp->fmt, and does nothing otherwise. It returns vp->sval in all cases.
